newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada drops in economic freedom, study says.
newsitem.headline: Canada drops in economic freedom, study says.

text.p: Canada has dropped five notches to rank 14th among the most economically free nations in the world, said a study released on Tuesday by a Canadian economic research organization.
In a study of 115 countries, the right-leaning Fraser Institute awarded Canada a 6.9 mark out of a possible score of 10.
The institute based its ratings on 17 factors that measure levels of basic economic freedoms, such as freedom of exchange, freedom to keep one's earnings and freedom to own private property.
In 1995, Canada was rated the ninth most economically free country.

"Canada's loss in position was due to the significant increases in economic freedom in Costa Rica, Australia, Panama, The Philippines and Mauritius, all of which were less free than Canada in last year's measurements," said Michael Walker, the Fraser Institute's executive director.

The results concluded that Hong Kong continues to be the most economically free country in the world. Singapore moves into second place, New Zealand ranks third, the United States fourth and Mauritius is in fifth place.

The top fifth of the countries in the study enjoyed average per capita GDP of C$20,412 (US$14,829), while the bottom fifth boasted average per capita GDP of only C$3,498 (US$2,451), the institute reported.
